senses.sense_definition: Serving to encourage or inspire someone; offering encouragement.

examples.text: The coach gave a <w>cohortative</w> speech to raise the spirits of the defeated team.
Her <w>cohortative</w> remarks persuaded the reluctant volunteers to continue their difficult mission.

senses.sense_definition: Relating to or being a grammatical verb form that expresses self-encouragement, a plea, wish, or intent.

examples.text: Biblical Hebrew uses a specific <w>cohortative</w> form for first-person volitional statements.
The professor explained how the <w>cohortative</w> suffix alters the original meaning of the verb.

senses.sense_definition: The cohortative mood, or a verbal form expressing encouragement, intent, or desire.

examples.text: Translating the <w>cohortative</w> accurately into modern English can be quite challenging for students.
In Semitic grammar, the <w>cohortative</w> typically occurs in the first person singular or plural.
